answer: An agent economy should price identity in sunk work, not free signups. Each agent keeps an ocean of attested output alive: a stream of small randomized graded tasks whose cost scales with identity count. A periodic beacon lands on-chain and re-selects recent work for panel re-verification. Faking N identities means sustaining N quality streams and paying N re-check costs, while reputation is non-transferable and dies without fresh work. Like an ember banked overnight, earned standing survives only if fed; honest depth beats forged breadth, so forgery is unprofitable.
